Christmas Choral Tots

Saturday 28 November 10am

Get into the festive spirit with this fun and interactive concert for 0-5 year-olds and their parents/carers.

Tickets Plan your visit

  • Doors open at 9.45am

    Location: St James’s Church, Piccadilly, London Ticket pricing: Adult £10/Child £5

    • Join Genesis Sixteen alumni singers on an interactive adventure full of singing and storytelling as we explore music about winter and Christmas. Expect to be delighted by festive songs old and new! Tots and their parents/carers will be invited to join in with festive songs, parachute and scarf activities, as well as having the opportunity to listen to some musical numbers performed by the Genesis Sixteen singers.

Nicole Wu (piano)

Wednesday 25 November 1.10pm

First Prize winner of the 2026 Guildhall Romantic Piano Prize and Second Prize at the 2026 Sheepdrove Piano Competition, Canadian pianist Nicole Wu has been recognized for her musical maturity, expressive depth, and stylistic versatility.

    Programme

    Claude Debussy: Pour le piano, L. 95
    I. Prélude
    II. Sarabande

    Artist Bio

    First Prize winner of the 2026 Guildhall Romantic Piano Prize and Second Prize at the 2026 Sheepdrove Piano Competition, Canadian pianist Nicole Wu has been recognized for her musical maturity, expressive depth, and stylistic versatility. Equally at home as a soloist and chamber musician, she has appeared across Europe and North America, earning recognition in numerous national and international competitions. Her distinctions include prizes at the Birmingham International Piano Competition, Eastbourne Young Soloist Competition, Prix d’Europe, OSM Competition, and the Canadian Music Competition.

    Nicole has performed in recitals at distinguished venues including Cliburn Hall in Texas, Milton Court Concert Hall in London, and the Musikverein in Vienna. Now based in London, she has presented solo recitals at venues such as St Stephen Walbrook and St James’s Church, with programmes spanning the Classical and Romantic repertoire alongside major
    twentieth-century works.

    An active participant in leading international festivals and academies, Nicole has worked with internationally renowned performers and pedagogues while broadening her artistic perspectives. Recent engagements include the Domaine Forget Academy, Orford Music Academy, the International Holland Music Sessions (2023), PianoTexas Young Artist Program (2024), the International Summer Academy (ISA) in Vienna, and the Gijón International Piano Festival (2026).

    Nicole is currently pursuing a Master of Music in Piano Performance at the Guildhall School of Music & Drama, where she studies with Professor Ronan O’Hora and Carole Presland on scholarship. Her graduate studies are generously supported by the Fishmongers’ Company and Steinway & Sons. She previously completed a Bachelor of Music at the Schulich School of Music of McGill University under the guidance of Dr. Ilya Poletaev. Throughout her studies, she has also received support from the Hnatyshyn Foundation and Jeunesses Musicales Canada. Her
    artistic development has been further enriched through masterclasses with distinguished musicians including Robert Levin, Kevin Kenner, Christopher Elton, Jan Jiráček von Arnim, Boris Berman, Norma Fisher, and Arie Vardi.

    Presented in association with Guildhall School of Music and Drama

    The Orion Trio was founded at Trinity Laban in 2025. Here performed at a masterclass with prominent pianist James Baillieu, in masterclass at the Piano Trio Society’s, and in concert at the Polish Hearth Club.

    Violinist Christina Schuetz completed an Artist Diploma, studying with Matthew Denton and Roman Mints. Trinity Laban previously awarded her a Professional Diploma with distinction in summer 2025. She has participated in the Lunigiana International Music Festival, the New Lights Contemporary Music Festival and various competitions at Trinity Laban. Previously, Christina was a solicitor in a City law firm.

    Cellist Sophie Baxter in an MMus graduate of Trinity Laban, where she studied with David Cohen and Sally Pendlebury. Previously, she read music at Durham University. She has a PGCE in group instrumental teaching from the London based charity ‘Music Masters’. She has been mentored by the London Symphony Orchestra and the orchestra of the Royal Opera House. She worked as a graduate assistant at Wells Cathedral School and the Purcell School.

    Alex Lukov completed a Master’s in Collaborative Piano, studying with Andrew Matthews-Owen, and working with string players and singers. He is a multi-instrumentalist, with advanced guitar and violin skills. Alex previously completed an undergraduate degree in astrophysics at University College London.

    Artist Bio

    Maria Linares, piano
    Spanish pianist María Linares has performed in consolidated Festivals and venues including CBSO Centre, Birmingham Symphony Hall, Steinway Hall in London and London Festival in the UK; II Iturbi Prize Festival, and Serenates Festival in Spain; Rossini Theatre in Gioia del Colle in Italy; and Vaduz Town Hall in Liechtenstein, among others. In January 2026, she released a CD with the Naxos label, performing a set of pieces by the composer Anton Urspruch. At the age of 12, she performed her first solo piano recital, later followed by playing as a soloist with orchestras such as the Valencian Orchestra, Youth Orchestra of Generalitat Valenciana, Youth Orchestra of Leon and Orchestra of the Royal Birmingham Conservatoire, in venues such as the Palau de Les Arts, Teatro Principal and Palau de la Música in Valencia, Palau Altea in Alicante, Palau de Congressos in Castellon and the Ciudad de León Auditorium, with conductors Manuel Hernández Silva, Roberto Forés, or Daniel Gil de Tejada.

    In addition to being named Music Ambassador for Spain by the Lang Lang Music Foundation, she has been supported by the Munster Trust, Craxton Memorial Trust, The Musicians’ Company, and in 2023 she was given the ‘Myra Hess’ award by HelpMusicians UK. Furthermore, she has been the main prize winner in the most distinguished competitions in her home country, part of them being VIPA 2022, Ciutat de Carlet 2022, XXVI Ruperto Chapí, XXXIV Marisa Montiel or XXVII Jacinto Guerrero. In the
    Royal Birmingham Conservatoire, she has also received the First Prize in competitions such as the Dennis Matthews, Renna Kellaway, or Beryl Chempin Beethoven Competition.
    Meanwhile, she has been selected to participate in several Masterclasses with renowned musicians such as Paul Badura-Skoda, Kirill Gerstein, Cyprien Katsaris, Michel Beroff or Claudio Martínez-Mehner. In addition to this, she has received scholarships from IMS Prussia Cove, Liechtenstein Intensive Weeks, Chetham’s International Piano Summer School, 29e Blonay Semaine Internationale de Piano or WSL Masterclasses. Maria has recently completed an Artist Diploma in the Royal College of Music under a full scholarship while being a Constant Kit and Lambert Junior Fellow, studying with Professors Norma Fischer and Danny Driver. Prior to this, she finished her bachelor’s and master’s Degrees with Distinction at the Royal Birmingham Conservatoire under full scholarships with Professor Pascal Nemirovski.

    Fabiola Sebastián, cello
    Fabiola Sebastián Guijarro was born in Madrid in 2002 and began her musical studies at the age of eight with Eduardo Palao in Alcalá de Henares. She graduated with honours from Madrid Royal Conservatory under the tutelage of Professor Fernando Arias. After completing her Master of Music in Performance with Distinction under Professor Richard Lester, she continued with an Artist Diploma under Professors Melissa Phelps and Richard Harwood, generously supported by the Carne Junior Fellowship and the Alvargonzález Foundation. She has been awarded several prizes, including Second Prize at the Soncello Competition, Second Prize at the Jaime Dobato Benavente Competition and Second Prize at the International Cello Competition Luthiers Clar. Since 2023, she has been a member of the Moment Piano Trio alongside Joan López and Javier Moyà, with whom she has been awarded First Prize at the Jesús de Monasterio Competition and Second Prize at the Arnuero International Chamber Music Competition. Her chamber music playing has been profoundly influenced by Helena Poggio (Quiroga Quartet), as well as the Sacconi Quartet and the Piatti Quartet. As an active chamber musician, she has performed at renowned venues and festivals, including the Ateneo de Madrid, Fundación Juan March, Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando, Santander International Festival, Sacconi Chamber Music Festival, Delta Chamber Music Festival and Mallorca Chamber Music Festival.

    She is a member of JONDE (Spanish National Youth Orchestra), with whom she has performed at the National Auditorium in Madrid, Palau de la Música in Valencia and Auditorio Princesa Leonor in Zaragoza. She has taken part in several RCM orchestral and ensemble projects, working with conductors such as Nicholas Collon, Douglas Boyd and Ben Palmer, as well as Kahchun Wong at the Queen Elizabeth Hall. Given her interest in contemporary music, she was selected to perform alongside the Next Ensemble at the Paris Conservatoire (CNSMDP) to celebrate the anniversary of Pierre Boulez. She has also participated in masterclasses with Alexander Baillie, Alisa Weilerstein, Gary Hoffman, Gregor Horsch, Marc Coppey, Paolo Bonomini, Rafael Rosenfeld, Robert Max and Sun-Won Yang, among others. Since October 2026, she has been a Fellow with Sinfonia Smith Square. She currently plays on a Roger Hansell Stradivarius copy, generously loaned to her by Moray Welsh.

    Artist Bio

    Bendit Chan is a Hong Kong-born pianist currently pursuing postgraduate studies at the Guildhall School of Music & Drama in London, where he studies with Gareth Owen and Noriko Ogawa.

    He has appeared as a concerto soloist at Cadogan Hall and Imperial College London, performing Rachmaninoff’s Piano Concerto No. 3 and Prokofiev’s Piano Concerto No. 3, and has also given solo and chamber performances in London. Alongside his solo work, Bendit is active as an orchestral pianist and chamber musician, and has performed across a broad range of repertoire.

    During his undergraduate studies at Imperial College London, where he completed a degree in Mathematics, he was awarded the Ede & Ravenscroft Music Bursary in recognition of his musical work. He is currently supported by a Guildhall School scholarship.

    Bendit continues to develop a wide-ranging solo repertoire while pursuing interests in chamber music, orchestral playing and collaborative performance.

    W.A Mozart:Andante & Variations in G major, K.501

    A. L. Dvorak: Selections from Legends, Op.59

    Artist Bio

    Lucas Saraiva Cunha (b. 2003) is a London-based pianist in his first year of MMus at Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance (TL), where he is a proud recipient of the Alfred and Therese Kitchin Scholarship and the Cardnell Piano Prize. He studies under the guidance of professor Yekaterina Lebedeva.

    Recent competitive successes include 1st Prize at the HGS Residents Association Intercollegiate Competition (London), 3rd Prize at the 34th Rome International Piano Competition, and recital prize by Musical Odyssey Masterclasses in Oxfordshire. He was a finalist in the Beethoven EPA intercollegiate competition.

    Lucas enjoys an active recital career. As a soloist, Lucas performs frequently across the UK and internationally, with notable appearances including a gala concert in Shunde, China, as part of celebrations for the 70th Anniversary of the Chinese Republic as well as solo recital in Megaron Concert Hall in Athens. Upcoming recitals include his debut in Germany at the Lev Natochenny Piano Festival in Bad Homburg.

    Lucas is particularly interested in expanding the classical concert tradition, integrating disciplines such as improvisation, dance, and theatre to create dynamic and engaging performances. A passionate advocate for contemporary music, he is frequently invited to perform at contemporary music festivals and to premiere works by composer contemporaries. Recent projects include performances of John Cage’s Sonatas and Interludes for Prepared Piano, alongside new works by himself and his peers written for the same preparation. His multifaceted artistic voice has led to collaborations with international organisations, including the Gina Bachauer International Music Association (Greece), which supports exceptionally talented young pianists. Additionally, Lucas curates a series of concerts at Winchmore School, in collaboration with other artists.

    In addition to his solo work, Lucas is an accomplished pianist in vocal repertoire, performing regularly at festivals within his conservatoire and across the UK, spanning repertoire from the Classical canon to works by Contemporary Female and Black British composers. As a committed chamber musician, he has performed at major London venues including Blackheath Halls, St James Piccadilly, and Kings Place. He was a Finalist in both the Oxford International Song Young Artists Programme and the Somerset Song Prize, where he received the award for Most Promising Young Pianist.

    Alique Khambatta is a pianist based in London. She completed her Master’s degree in Performance at Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance, where she studied with Elena Riu and Mikhail Kazakevich. She was supported during her postgraduate studies by the Satyam Kalon Scholarship. She previously completed her Bachelor of Music as a recipient of the Udmi Devi Scholarship.

    Alique began piano lessons at the age of five in India with Roxana Anklesaria at the Academy of Music, and has also been mentored by Myrna Fernandez. She has won numerous prizes at national and international competitions, including multiple awards at the Musiquest Competition and the International Trio Competition in Marktoberdorf, Germany. She has participated in masterclasses with artists including Joanna MacGregor, Jean-Efflam Bavouzet, Pascal Rogé, and Tomislav Baynov.

    Alique has performed widely across the UK and internationally, appearing at contemporary music festivals, in broadcast performances, and in concerts featuring commissioned works. She was previously an Artist in Residence at the London Transport Museum, where she presented a series of concerts with her singer duo partner. Her performance work encompasses both solo and collaborative projects, with an interest in presenting engaging and varied programmes to diverse audiences.

    Presented in association with Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance

Penglei Liang (soprano) & Yuyao Qu (piano)

A beautiful and varied voice and piano recital presented by the Royal College of Music with works by Debussy, Strauss, Florence Price and Verdi.

    Programme

    PART ONE · AWAKENING AND LONGING
    Claude Debussy (1862–1918)
    1. La Flûte de Pan, from Trois Chansons de Bilitis
    The first stirring of desire
    2. Green, from Ariettes oubliées
    Meeting the beloved; an offering of love

    Richard Strauss (1864–1949):
    3. Ständchen, Op. 17 No. 2
    A serenade; a meeting by night
    4. Freundliche Vision, Op. 48 No. 1
    A vision of the life they might share

    Jonathan Dove (b. 1959):
    5. Between Your Sheets
    Watching the beloved sleep

    Giuseppe Verdi (1813–1901):
    6. Caro nome, from Rigoletto
    Imagining a love not yet lived

    INTERLUDE · THREE SONGS BY FLORENCE PRICE
    Florence Price (1887–1953) was the first African-American woman to have a symphony played by a major American
    orchestra, when the Chicago Symphony gave her Symphony in E minor in 1933. Alongside the orchestral works she wrote
    more than a hundred songs, many of them settings of Black American poets. Much of her music disappeared after her death
    and was recovered only in 2009, when a large cache of manuscripts came to light in a derelict house outside Chicago. The two
    Langston Hughes settings here stand on either side of Night, a quiet nocturne.
    7. Songs to the Dark Virgin
    An ardent declaration
    Langston Hughes
    8. Night
    Tenderness and stillness in the dark
    Louise C. Wallace
    9. Hold Fast to Dreams
    Hold on, though the dream breaks
    Langston Hughes

    PART TWO · LOSS, LETTING GO, AND HOPE

    Gaetano Donizetti (1797–1848):
    10. Prendi, per me sei libero, from L’elisir d’amore
    Love turns; letting go, or testing

    arr. Benjamin Britten (1913–1976):
    11. The Last Rose of Summer
    An omen of fading

    Clara Schumann (1819–1896):
    12. Ich stand in dunklen Träumen, Op. 13 No. 1
    The beloved is lost

    Franz Schubert (1797–1828):
    13. An den Mond, D. 193
    Grief after parting

    Edvard Grieg (1843–1907):
    14. Ein Traum, from Sechs Lieder, Op. 48
    It was only a dream

    Strauss:
    15. Morgen!, Op. 27 No. 4
    And tomorrow the sun will shine again

     

    Artist Bio

    Soprano Penglei Liang recently completed a Master of Performance at the Royal College of Music, supported by the Audrey Sacher Award, where she studied with Jeffrey Stewart. She also holds a Master’s degree in Musicology from the University of Edinburgh.

    Penglei debuted as a soloist in Orff’s Carmina Burana in Oxford, and has since appeared as the soloist in Rossini’s Petite Messe Solennelle, Saint-Saëns’ Oratorio de Noël in London and Aylesbury. She performed as concert soloist at the National Liberal Club, and at the Silk Road Concert supported by the Chinese Embassy. Operatic roles include Laoula (L’étoile), Elmira (Sosarme), Hélène (Véronique) and Elisetta (Il Matrimonio Segreto). Penglei joined the Grasmere Song 2025 with scholarship, where she had masterclass with Sir Thomas Allen. She participated in the RCM Song Plus Program, and received a masterclass with Pumeza Matshikiza. Her ensemble and chorus performances include Holst’s The Planets at the 2024 BBC Proms at the Royal Albert Hall, Madama Butterfly at St. John’s Smith Square, and Le Nozze di Figaro with the RCM Opera Studio. Penglei performed as a concert soloist at the 2026 Great Malvern Festival of Singing. She will be singing as soprano soloist for Handel’s Messiah in November.

    Yuyao Qu is a collaborative pianist of rare sensitivity and musical depth, celebrated for her refined artistry in art song and chamber music. Born in Dalian, China, she brings to her performances a distinctive perspective shaped by early immersion in a wide range of artistic disciplines — dance, vocal music, painting, ikebana, and calligraphy — an interdisciplinary background that continues to inform the nuance and poetry of her musical expression.

    Recent highlights include appearances at the Grasmere Song Festival in England’s Lake District and the Ticino Musica Festival 2025 in Lugano, Switzerland, where she performed as a sponsored participant in a series of chamber music concerts and masterclasses. She serves as featured collaborative pianist for the New Elements Music Concert Series 2025–2026 in London and the Qingxiang Music Season 2025 at Shuimu Theatre in Beijing, collaborating with distinguished singers and instrumentalists in programmes spanning art song and chamber music.
    Her international concert appearances span Birmingham Symphony Hall; St James’s Church Piccadilly, St Dunstan-in-the-West, the Austrian Cultural Forum, St John the Baptist Church, and St Bride’s Church in London; Elisarion Cultural Centre in Switzerland; Chongqing Philharmonic Music Factory and Nanjing Steinway & Sons Music Centre in China; and Fulkerson Recital Hall and Warner Music Hall in the United States, among others.

    Yuyao has studied with Simon Lepper, Kathron Sturrock, Colin Stone, and Ran Dank. She completed her Artist Diploma in Collaborative Piano at the Royal College of Music in 2024, her Master of Arts in Piano at the Royal Academy of Music, and her Bachelor of Music with Honours at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music. She has participated in masterclasses with Sir Thomas Allen, Nicky Spence OBE, Audrey Hyland, James Holmes, Paulina Tukiainen, Susan Manoff, and Ulrich Koella. Her repertoire encompasses an extensive range of German and French art song alongside diverse chamber music works. She is the recipient of the Gold Prize in Chamber Music at the London Young Musicians Competition.
    Alongside her performing career, Yuyao maintains an active presence as a freelance collaborative pianist, piano educator, and associate accompanist at the Royal College of Music and Eltham College, where she continues to explore the intersection of artistry and music education.

    Presented in association with Royal College of Music

    Artist Bio

    Simo Šiševic is a distinguished Montenegrin pianist a Master degree student at the Royal Academy of Music in the class of the renowned Tatiana Sarkissova.
    Šišević graduated from `the Royal College of Music with First Class Honours where he studied with Gordon Fergus-Thompson and John Byrne. Furthermore, he currently studies with Boris Berman at the Accademia del Riddoto here he undertakes his master’s degree. During his undergraduate studies he studied the harpsichord with Jane Chapman and fortepiano with Geoffrey Govier.

    His recent concerts with Montenegrin Symphony Orchestra and the Festival Orchestra of KotorArt with whom he performed Beethoven’s Triple Concerto and Shostakovich’s First Piano Concerto have had great reviews and standing ovations.

    Šišević performs extensively in the UK and Europe.He gave recitals at festivals such as KotorArt, Grad Teatar Budva, Barski Ljetopis, Dani muzike Herceg Novi, Skopsko leto, and halls such as Amaryllis Fleming Concert Hall, Europe House, Duke’s Hall, St James’s Church Piccadilly, St Mary’s Perivale Church, St Mary Abbots Church, University Women’s Club, English-Speaking Union, Austrian Cultural Forum, Museum of Macedonian Struggle, KIC Budo Tomovic. In 2016, Šišević represented his country and its musical heritage in the “Monténégro au coeur de l’Europe” concert at the Festival ‘Weekend de Clavier Contemporain’ at the Frédéric Chopin Conservatoire in Paris. At the age of 17, he had his debut with an orchestra when he played Mozart’s D-major concerto.

    Šišević’s competition successes include: Third Prize at the Carles and Sofia Piano Competition in Spain (2021), Second Prize at the Orbetello Piano Competition in Orbetello, Italy (2021), First Prize in the Pieter Gaci Competition in Shkoder, Albania. (2017), First Prize at the International Piano Competition in Tivat, Montenegro (2016), Special Prize at the Windsor Piano Competition (2015), Absolute Prize in the Academy Award Competition in Rome (2013).

    In 2019 he formed a trio with Luka Perazić and Kosta Popović that gave lots of concerts so far. During the same year he took part in the “Made in New York” festival and played alongside Randy Brecker, Bobby Sanabria, and Edsel Gomez. On numerous occasions, he has collaborated with a famous soprano Tamara Radjenovic. The famous Milos Karadaglic Foundation selected Šišević as their scholar for the 2024/25 season and award him with a scholarship.

    Šišević has been generously supported by the Salomon Family, The Kathleen Trust, The Zetland Foundation, Talent Unlimited, Petrovic-Njegos foundation, The Henry Wood Trust, St Marylebone Educational Foundation, PAM Montenegro, Ministry of Culture of Montenegro, Municipality of City of Bar and Capital City of Podgorica, Global Ports Holding. He was awarded a scholarship by Montenegrin Ministry of Education and Culture.

    Since 2021, he is a Global Talent Visa holder, a visa endowed by the Arts Council England for exceptional achievements and contribution to arts.
    Humanitarian work and volunteering is an important part of his life, as he has taken part in multiple actions by the UNICEF, Save the Children, Njegos Foundation, the Lifeline and the Royal Family of Yugoslavia in raising funds for orphanages, hospital equipment and the less fortunate.

    Simo Šišević was born in Montenegro. Received first piano lesson at the “Njegos” school in Bar with Mr Maja Basarab. He is a graduate of the Art School of Music and Ballet in Podgorica, where he studied with the famous Anka Asanović. Later he was one of the last students of Vladimir Bochkaryov.

    Presented in association with Talent Unlimited

    Christmas for All – A Place for Everyone

    At Christmas, St James’s is a place where everyone is welcome. For people facing loneliness, homelessness, poor mental health, financial hardship or displacement, our doors can offer something as simple – and as important – as a warm welcome, practical support and a place where they are known and treated with dignity.

    Your donation can help keep St James’s open and welcoming to all this Christmas. Your gift supports hot meals, practical assistance, mental health support, refugee and asylum seeker support, and the staff and volunteers who make this work possible. Together, we can make sure that nobody who comes through our doors is turned away.

    Please consider making a donation to Christmas for All and help make St James’s a place for everyone.

    Artist Bio

    Follia 4 is a London-based recorder ensemble dedicated to expanding the recorder’s role in contemporary music. Through innovative, accessible performances, the ensemble aims to connect with audiences and showcase the instrument’s expressive potential in new and exciting ways.

    The ensemble comprises Lizzie Knatt, Otto Hashmi, Hannah Parry, and Rowena Jones.

    In April 2026, Follia 4 premiered bellyfull of glowsong for recorder quartet and fixed electronics by composer Thomas Shorthouse at the annual festival of the Society of Recorder Players. The work transforms fragments of a Yorkshire folk song into an intensely cyclical, mesmeric, chant-like texture. As Shorthouse writes, “bellyfull of glowsong reflects on the importance of the communal musical experience, its almost magical ability to bring people together and sustain musical traditions.”

    Presented in association with Royal Academy of Music

The Flarra Duo is a partnership of flautist Penny Cairney-Leeming and harpist/composer Hannah Runting, described as ‘uncannily luminous’ and ‘bold and fearless’ respectively.

    Programme

    Hannah Runting – The Songbird – i. Dawn, ii. Midday, iii. Dusk, iv. Midnight

    Arnold Bax – Sonata for Flute and Harp – i. Allegro Moderato, ii. Lento, iii. Moderato Giocoso

    Artist Bio

    The Flarra Duo is a partnership of flautist Penny Cairney-Leeming and harpist/composer Hannah Runting, described as ‘uncannily luminous’ and ‘bold and fearless’ respectively. Together, they have performed at Regent Hall, various venues within the Royal Academy of Music, and most recently, St Marylebone Parish Church in partnership with Wigmore Hall for their ‘Music for the Moment’ series.

    This featured a program of new and well-loved works for an audience of people living with dementia and their carers. Through their work together, Flarra Duo forges connections with audiences, devising innovative performances and pushing the boundaries of compositional and performance practices.
    Penny’s soloist debut saw her perform the Mozart Flute and Harp concerto at the Barbican, and her chamber music partnerships with award-winning Zephyr Flutes and the Notus Trio (flute, viola, harp) are testament to her experience and passion for working collaboratively. Penny is also an advocate for contemporary music, premiering multiple new works, and recently performing in the Royal Academy of Music’s Boulez Anniversary concert.

    Hannah, a current scholar of the Riot Ensemble ‘Arts Mentor Lucerne’ scheme, is equally passionate about contemporary music. She recently premiered Shin Kim’s concerto ‘Dream Poem’ on BBC Radio 3, performed Boulez’s ‘Sur Incises’ with the Manson Ensemble, and the UK premiere of Rolf Hind’s critically acclaimed opera, ‘Sky in a Small Cage’. She is also the harpist for Paraorchestra, a disability championing organisation that has seen her perform at the BBC Proms, Dublin National Concert Hall and the Southbank Centre.
    As a composer, her projects have achieved multiple sold out performances, and her works often feature in Flarra Duo programming.

Music for All Saints and All Souls

Tuesday 27 October 7pm

World renowned choir The Sixteen perform some of the finest choral music of the Portuguese and English Renaissance.

Tickets Plan your visit

  • St James’s aspires to be a place where all can belong, and where every person’s gifts and identities are welcome and celebrated. We are working to improve the experience at St James’s in the church building and the online community. We have step-free access from the courtyard to the church, and a toilet for disabled people. The courtyard and Redemption Roasters coffee shop are wheelchair accessible.

    • Experience the extraordinary sound of The Sixteen as the world-renowned choir performs a programme of some of the finest choral music of the Portuguese and English Renaissance.

    Featuring works by Francisco Lôbo, Tomás Luis de Victoria, William Byrd, William Harris, Charles Villiers Stanford and Hubert Parry, the programme explores music written for All Saints and All Souls, from the luminous polyphony of the Renaissance to Parry’s deeply moving Lord, let me know mine end.

    The concert continues The Sixteen’s new partnership with St James’s Church, Piccadilly, bringing exceptional choral music into our historic setting.
